closureRequires: all medium findings fixed or documented as later-stage boundaries

controls.requirement: No tracked .env or credential-bearing environment file other than .env.example.
Generated build/test output is ignored and not tracked.
No one-shot Stage 5/6/7 patch/bootstrap workflow or temporary patch script remains tracked.
Publication fixtures remain neutral and imported private reference material remains absent.
npm dependency audit fails CI at low severity or above.
Session tokens are cryptographically random and only AUTH_SECRET-keyed token hashes are persisted server-side.
Session cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite, Secure in production, root-scoped, and time-bounded.
Password hashes use bcrypt with an intentional work factor of at least 12.
Login failure remains non-enumerating and abuse-limited.
Registration is closed by default in production.
Browser cross-origin login, registration, and logout requests are rejected.
Authentication email/password inputs are length-bounded.
Expired in-memory authentication rate-limit buckets are periodically pruned rather than retained indefinitely.
Unauthenticated bootstrap and sync access is rejected.
Browser cross-origin workspace mutation requests are rejected.
All API responses are explicitly no-store at the HTTP header layer.
Database unavailability is surfaced structurally without raw database exceptions.
Demo reset is production-disabled unless ALLOW_DEMO_RESET is explicitly true.
Sync request bytes, mutation count, payload bytes, IDs, and field-key lengths are bounded.
Byte limits use UTF-8 bytes and reject oversized multibyte payloads.
Upsert entityId must equal payload.id.
Synchronization timestamps are bounded and parseable.
Cross-user record and relationship references are rejected.
Mutation IDs are unique per user.
Accepted mutation replay is idempotent.
Stale mutations are surfaced and do not silently overwrite newer server state.
Local workspace and outbox commit atomically.
Legacy delete-operation no-op is documented and not redefined before Stage 9 lifecycle semantics.
Local workspace and outbox are scoped by verified user identity.
Legacy local-store migration cannot mix users.
Offline startup refuses to guess among multiple local identities.
Offline startup without a previously verified local workspace is blocked clearly.
Client local-storage implementation never persists passwords, session tokens, AUTH_SECRET, or reusable server credentials.
Offline-ready UI is backed by a complete verified shell manifest.
API responses are absent from shell caches and never replaced by HTML shell fallback.
Previously authenticated workspace cold-reopens offline.
Core and dynamic project routes cold-open and hard-refresh offline.
Pending local edits survive offline hard reload.
Back/forward and search-to-record routing remain local while offline.
Production CSP excludes unsafe-eval.
Frame, MIME, referrer, permissions, opener/resource isolation headers are present.
Production HSTS is explicit.
Shell caches are versioned and old caches are removed only after new-shell verification.
Health response is public, minimal, and no-store.
Every user-owned primary model is explicitly user-scoped.
Sync ownership checks cover target records and relationship references.
Prisma validate/generate/migrate/seed run against disposable PostgreSQL in CI.
Backup/restore and rollback rehearsal remain explicitly unclaimed until performed.
Mobile hit-target, menu semantics, keyboard/editor and long-title tests remain green.
Offline, pending-sync, conflict and shell-readiness states remain visible.
Network-required actions fail explicitly while offline.
Local-first contract, project state, security and deployment docs do not overclaim production or offline scope.
Deployment environment switches include registration, demo reset, canonical origin and auth secret guidance.
Final stage report distinguishes automated evidence from later operational work.
CI includes dependency audit, Stage 7 static audit, Prisma, typecheck, build, production browser matrix, and development browser suite.
Production/offline tests run against next start rather than development HMR runtime.
Stage 7 closes only on a full green branch run with exact test counts recorded.
